annotations.title: Recommend an AI tool for a task

description: Pick the best AI tools for a job the user wants done. Call this whenever a user asks which AI tool, app or service to use ("what should I use to transcribe my podcast?", "is there an AI that makes pitch decks?", "best free logo maker"), or when you need a tool to finish their task and do not already know a current one. Pass the job in plain words, plus any budget, platform, must-have features and tools to leave out. Returns up to 3 picks from EveryAI's 2,700+ reviewed listings, each with why it fits (quoted from its listing), pricing as stated, a link to give the user, a 0-100 data-quality score and a last-verified date, plus the alternatives considered and why they ranked lower. Ranking is by fit and data quality only: payment never changes rank, and a paid placement can only appear separately as "sponsored" with sponsored:true. Fewer than 3 picks (or none) means nothing else fits: say so instead of guessing. Do not use it to look up one named tool (get_tool) or to browse a category (search_tools).

budget.description: "free", or the most the user will pay per month in USD (20, "$20/month"). Tools whose listing states a higher price, or no free option when "free", are left out. Tools with a confirmed price are picked first; one that states no price is only offered when fewer than three confirmed tools fit, marked unconfirmed. pricing.stated_by says whether a price is from the maker, auto-detected, or read from listing text.

exclude.description: Tools to leave out (ones the user already tried or ruled out), by name, slug or website.

must_have.description: Features the tool must mention on its listing, a few words each, e.g. ["speaker labels", "SRT export"]. A tool missing any of them is not picked.

platform.description: Where it has to run or what it has to plug into: ios, android, mobile, chrome, mac, windows, linux, desktop, web, api, mcp, cli, vscode, slack, discord, telegram, whatsapp, wordpress, shopify, figma, notion, self_hosted, or any other product name. Only tools whose listing mentions it are picked ("web" is not enforced: most listed tools are web apps).

task.description: What the user wants to get done, in plain words, e.g. "transcribe podcast episodes with speaker labels" or "write cold outreach emails for B2B sales". Describe the job, not a product name; leave out names, emails and other personal details.
